content: Famotidine is an oral medication that functions as an inhibitor of gastric acid secretion. It is FDA-approved for the treatment of conditions such as heartburn, gastric hypersecretion, gastric ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and indigestion. Common side effects include constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, and headache. Adult Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications and Dosage (Adults) Indications: Famotidine is indicated for the treatment of duodenal ulcers, esophagitis, GERD, gastric hypersecretion, gastric ulcers, and indigestion. Dosage: To relieve symptoms, swallow one tablet with a glass of water. Do not chew the tablet. To prevent symptoms, swallow one tablet with a glass of water 10 to 60 minutes before consuming food or beverages that cause heartburn. Do not exceed two tablets in 24 hours. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Adults) Indications: Off-label uses include maintenance therapy for esophagitis, gastritis, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, stress ulcers, and urticaria. Dosage: For acute duodenal ulcer disease: 40 mg orally once daily at bedtime or 20 mg orally twice daily. For maintenance of duodenal ulcer disease: 20 mg orally once daily at bedtime. For short-term treatment of GERD: 20 to 40 mg orally twice daily for up to 12 weeks. For gastric hypersecretion: 20 to 160 mg orally every 6 hours. For acute gastric ulcers: 40 mg orally once daily at bedtime. For short-term symptom treatment of GERD: 20 mg orally twice daily for up to 6 weeks. For indigestion: 10 to 20 mg orally twice daily. Pediatric Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications and Dosage (Pediatrics) Indications: Famotidine is indicated for duodenal ulcers, esophagitis, GERD, gastric hypersecretion, gastric ulcers, and indigestion in pediatric patients. Dosage: For children aged 12 years and older: To relieve symptoms, swallow one tablet with a glass of water. Do not chew the tablet. To prevent symptoms, swallow one tablet with a glass of water 10 to 60 minutes before consuming food or beverages that cause heartburn. Do not exceed two tablets in 24 hours. For children under 12 years: Consult a doctor. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Pediatrics) Guideline-Supported Use: Limited information is available. A typical dosage is 5 mg/kg/day orally at bedtime or divided into two doses daily, with a maximum dose of 40 mg/day. Contraindications Do not use famotidine if you are allergic to it or other acid reducers. Do not use if you experience difficulty or pain swallowing food, vomiting blood, or have bloody or black stools, as these may indicate a serious condition. Consult a doctor. Avoid use in patients with kidney disease unless under the advice and supervision of a doctor. Warnings If you have had heartburn for more than three months, consult a doctor, as this may indicate a more serious condition. Seek medical advice if you experience heartburn with lightheadedness, sweating, or dizziness; chest pain or shoulder pain with shortness of breath, sweating, or pain spreading to arms, neck, or shoulders; frequent chest pain; frequent wheezing with heartburn; unexplained weight loss; nausea or vomiting; or stomach pain. Discontinue use and consult a doctor if heartburn persists or worsens, or if you need to use the product for more than 14 days. If pregnant or breastfeeding, consult a healthcare professional before use. Keep out of reach of children. In case of overdose, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Experience Common: Constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, headache. Serious: Dermatologic: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (very rare), toxic epidermal necrolysis (very rare). Gastrointestinal: Necrotizing enterocolitis in fetuses or newborns. Immunologic: Anaphylaxis (infrequent), angioedema (infrequent). Musculoskeletal: Rhabdomyolysis. Neurologic: Seizures (rare). Respiratory: Interstitial pneumonia (infrequent), nosocomial pneumonia. Postmarketing Experience Limited information is available regarding postmarketing experience with famotidine. Drug Interactions Limited information is available regarding drug interactions with famotidine. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: There is no FDA or Australian Drug Evaluation Committee (ADEC) guidance on the use of famotidine in pregnant women. Labor and Delivery: No FDA guidance is available on the use of famotidine during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: No FDA guidance is available on the use of famotidine in nursing mothers. Pediatric Use: No FDA guidance is available on the use of famotidine in pediatric patients. Geriatric Use: No FDA guidance is available on the use of famotidine in geriatric patients. Gender and Race: No FDA guidance is available on the use of famotidine in specific gender or racial populations. Renal and Hepatic Impairment: No FDA guidance is available on the use of famotidine in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Immunocompromised Patients: No FDA guidance is available on the use of famotidine in immunocompromised patients. Administration and Monitoring Administration: Famotidine is administered orally. Clinical Studies Limited information is available regarding clinical studies of famotidine. Storage Store famotidine at 20°C to 25°C (68°F to 77°F). Protect from moisture and light. Precautions with Alcohol The interaction between alcohol and famotidine has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication.
